papers.title: Dynamic chromatin tethering of MDC1 regulates genome stability.
papers.summary: The proline-serine-threonine repeat region of MDC1 acts as a multivalent nucleosome-binding domain. Constitutive chromatin association supports RAD51 loading and homologous recombination in interphase, while mitotic phosphorylation attenuates binding, preventing aberrant chromosome interactions while the MDC1-TopBP1-CIP2A complex maintains DNA tethering and genome stability.

papers.title: ProRB: a structure-free unified framework for joint prediction and design of protein-RNA interactions.
papers.summary: ProRB is a unified sequence-based framework that jointly predicts protein-RNA binding affinity and interfaces and generates protein-binding RNA sequences. Fusing protein and RNA language-model embeddings via cross-modal attention, it matches or beats structure-based methods, reveals motif-centric binding logic, and enables design of RNA therapeutics.

papers.title: Complementation of a human disease phenotype by intercellular mRNA transfer.
papers.summary: mRNAs transferred between cells through tunneling nanotubes are translated in recipient cells and can complement genetic defects: co-culturing Zellweger patient PEX6-mutant fibroblasts or PEX5-knockout cells with wild-type cells restores peroxisome biogenesis. Complementation occurs via TNT-mediated mRNA transfer, not exosomes or protein transfer, suggesting new mRNA therapeutic approaches.

papers.title: PPM1L-dependent PD-L1 dephosphorylation orchestrates tumor-type-specific ubiquitin ligase recognition to govern its degradation.
papers.summary: PPM1L-regulated PD-L1 phosphorylation dictates recognition by distinct E3 ubiquitin ligases (ARIH1, RING1, RNF2), driving proteasomal degradation in a cancer-type-dependent manner. SerpinB1 relieves ARIH1 autoinhibition, promoting PD-L1 ubiquitination. PPM1L deficiency synergizes with anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in mouse models, informing precision immunotherapy strategies.

papers.title: Pathogenic KIF1A variants differentially disrupt axonal trafficking and impede synaptic development.
papers.summary: Using isogenic human iPSC-derived neurons, distinct pathogenic KIF1A mutations differentially disrupt axonal trafficking: null and hypoactive variants delay neurite outgrowth, mislocalize synaptic cargoes, and reduce synapse density, while a hyperactive variant causes aberrant synaptic vesicle precursor motility and presynaptic patterning deficits, explaining KIF1A-associated neurological disorder severity.

papers.title: EPHA2/CD44-directed trafficking enhances endosomal leakiness and antisense therapy delivery.
papers.summary: Antisense oligonucleotide engagement of the scavenger receptor CD44 activates the ERK-RSK axis to phosphorylate EPHA2, enabling ASO endocytosis and trafficking into nuclear-captured endosomes. These endosomes undergo lipid peroxidation and become leaky, letting ASOs escape and suppress target mRNAs; blocking stress granule-mediated repair enhances ASO effectiveness.

papers.title: Rhoptry biogenesis in Plasmodium sporozoites is uncoupled from mitosis and forms distinct pairs.
papers.summary: Using mosquito tissue ultrastructure expansion microscopy, the authors establish a timeline of rhoptry biogenesis in Plasmodium sporozoites, showing rhoptry pairs form uncoupled from mitosis, are consumed during salivary gland invasion, and are specialized for different invasion events. RON11 is the first protein implicated; disruption blocks parasite transmission.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal regulation of DNA repair proteins between Golgi and nucleus maintains genome stability.
papers.summary: Human Protein Atlas localization data revealed DNA damage response proteins occupying distinct Golgi compartments that redistribute to the nucleus upon genotoxic stress. ATM-dependent release of giantin-tethered RAD51C enables nuclear import and repair foci; giantin depletion causes aberrant foci and genome instability, positioning the Golgi as a DDR coordination node.

papers.title: Nanoscale junctional membrane curvatures recruit BIN1 and SNX9 for endothelial collective migration.
papers.summary: Cryo-SIM and FIB-SEM revealed nanoscale membrane folds at asymmetric adherens junctions of migrating endothelial cells. BAR domain proteins BIN1 and SNX9 are recruited to these curvatures in distinct phases, regulating front-rear polarity of follower cells; SNX9 depletion disturbs VE-cadherin dynamics and sheet migration in zebrafish.

papers.title: CAST/ELKS-endophilin-A interaction ensures synaptic vesicle pool size.
papers.summary: Active zone proteins CAST and ELKS maintain synaptic vesicle pool size through direct interaction with endophilin-A family proteins. Disrupting CAST-endophilin-A binding in cultured hippocampal neurons reduced releasable vesicles, mislocalized endophilin-A, and altered presynaptic clathrin light chain localization, redefining active zone roles beyond structural organization.

papers.title: GCL pruning of PIP3 establishes the soma-germline boundary.
papers.summary: In Drosophila embryos, Germ cell-less (GCL) degrades the receptor Torso to enable primordial germ cell formation. Torso activates PI3K, generating PIP3-enriched membrane domains that suppress PGC formation; GCL clears PIP3, enabling myosin II enrichment and establishing the soma-germline boundary through cortical lipid organization.

papers.title: PAK4 promotes vertex remodeling to maintain epithelial integrity and barrier function.
papers.summary: Junctional kinase PAK4 accumulates at multicellular vertices in MDCK cells and Xenopus embryos, recruited by the scaffolding protein afadin. PAK4 inhibition increased higher-order vertices, junctional discontinuities, and barrier defects with abnormal junctional myosin II accumulation, indicating PAK4 and afadin cooperate to maintain epithelial integrity via vertex remodeling.

papers.title: Kinetochore clustering is mediated by Mps1 phosphorylation of conserved MELT motifs in Stu1.
papers.summary: In budding yeast, the Mps1 kinase phosphorylates two conserved MELT motifs in Stu1 to recruit Slk19 and cluster unattached kinetochores, promoting microtubule capture. Structural analysis of the Stu1:Slk19 complex reveals string-like filaments, suggesting kinetochore capture regulation is a conserved Mps1 function across eukaryotes.

papers.title: PISD acts as a switch between lipophagy and fatty acid transfer to mitochondria.
papers.summary: The lipid droplet-localized PISD-LD isoform of phosphatidylserine decarboxylase mediates lipid droplet-mitochondria contacts, recruiting ATG2A/B for fatty acid transfer while binding spartin to inhibit lipophagy. Disrupting these contacts activates lipophagy; PISD-LD thus switches between droplet-to-mitochondria fatty acid transfer and lipophagic lipid degradation.

papers.title: Rag GTPases and mTORC1 regulate intestinal stem cell activity in response to nutrient availability.
papers.summary: In Drosophila, inhibiting Rag GTPases in enterocytes triggers MITF activation and Upd3 expression, stimulating JAK-STAT signaling to boost intestinal stem cell proliferation and differentiation. mTORC1 inactivation activates the same axis via a MITF-independent mechanism, showing nutrient sensing in enterocytes non-cell-autonomously regulates stem cell activity.

papers.title: Intercellular mitochondrial transfer and trans-mitophagy in response to protein import dysfunction.
papers.summary: Bidirectional mitochondrial trafficking through tunnelling nanotubes rescues protein import failure. Transferred import-defective mitochondria fragment and undergo lysosomal degradation, while ROS-producing mitochondria from import-competent cells transfer into failing neighbors and accumulate in previously uncharacterized mitochondrial degradation bodies, suggesting cooperative conventional and noncanonical trans-mitophagy restores mitochondrial function.

papers.title: aPKC exclusion from the apical cortex in enteroblasts maintains stem cell homeostasis in Drosophila.
papers.summary: In the Drosophila midgut, smooth septate junction proteins drive apical aPKC loss during enteroblast differentiation. In their absence, aPKC persists apically and intestinal stem cells overproliferate, linked through kibra's aPKC-binding domain to Hippo/Misshapen-Yorkie signaling. Antagonism between aPKC and junctional proteins maintains stem cell homeostasis.

papers.title: Meiotic CENP-C supports centromere assembly and kinetochore recruitment in spermatogenesis.
papers.summary: In Drosophila male meiosis, CENP-C functions with CAL1 to maintain centromeres in early prophase I. In late prophase, CENP-C becomes dispensable for maintenance but is crucial for kinetochore recruitment and post-meiosis II CID (CENP-A) assembly independently of CAL1, revealing distinct functional protein pools in spermatogenesis.

papers.title: PIKfyve influences inter-organelle contacts with lysosomes to modulate the endoplasmic reticulum.
papers.summary: PIKfyve converts PI3P to PI(3,5)P2 and promotes lysosome fission. Its inhibition causes perinuclear clustering of less motile lysosomes that arrests ER hitchhiking, plus hyper-tethering of protrudin to lysosomes via excess PI3P, distorting ER morphology. PIKfyve thus balances phosphoinositides at ER-lysosome contact sites.

papers.title: Why atypical findings matter: Follow up testing finds diagnostic results related to cfDNA screen.
papers.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
papers.summary: Across ten years, 204 index cases with atypical cfDNA screens underwent follow-up testing; 102 had diagnostic findings, 87 related to the screen. Copy number variants were most common, then aneuploidy and rearrangements; uniparental disomy and consanguinity also appeared. Invasive testing clarifies atypical results for fetus and pregnant person.

papers.title: Activating a novel cell death pathway to target PI-resistant multiple myeloma and enhance immunogenic cell death.
papers.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
papers.summary: Anwulignan, a natural product, retains activity against proteasome inhibitor-resistant multiple myeloma. It directly targets nucleophosmin 1, inducing cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, and activates caspase-1-dependent gasdermin D pyroptosis, driving immunogenic cell death. In syngeneic models it expanded T cells and improved tumor control, supporting dual-function therapeutic potential.

papers.title: KDM2B controls HIF levels and activity through its JmjC and CxxC domains.
papers.summary: KDM2B regulates HIF activity in a cell-type-dependent manner: depletion decreases HIF activity in U2OS and MDA-MB-231 cells but increases it in HeLa. KDM2B requires its JmjC demethylase and CxxC DNA-binding domains, supports RNA polymerase II recruitment to HIF1A, and enables proliferation under hypoxia.

papers.title: Blood flow coordinates collective endothelial cell migration during vascular plexus formation and promotes angiogenic sprout regression via vegfr3/flt4.
papers.summary: In zebrafish, blood flow coordinates collective endothelial migration in the sub-intestinal venous plexus, opposing continuous ventral migration and driving angiogenic sprout regression. Non-perfused sprouts regress as cells migrate against flow into the vein; regression under low flow requires VEGFR3/FLT4, showing how flow sculpts vascular remodeling.

papers.title: Exploring the Substrate Selectivity of the Condensation Domain VibH through Engineered Adenylation Domains, Non-Native Amide Synthesis, and Substrate Recognition Analysis.
papers.summary: Systematic analysis of the VibH condensation domain, bypassing A-domain constraints with engineered EntE variants, revealed stringent donor-site specificity for dihydroxybenzoic acid-like substrates but broad, distance-dependent acceptor-site amine tolerance. This asymmetric recognition architecture enabled synthesis of non-native amide conjugates and a framework for rational NRPS reprogramming.

papers.title: Exploiting Acquired Drug Resistance in Pancreatic Cancer through Selective Covalent Targeting of MAP2K4/7.
papers.summary: In KRASG12D-driven pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, full JNK pathway inactivation via combined MAP2K4/MAP2K7 inhibition restores sensitivity to KRAS inhibition in resistant cells by disabling the feedback loop that reactivates KRAS signaling. Inhibitor-sensitive cells gain no benefit, revealing a resistance-specific vulnerability amenable to therapeutic exploitation.

papers.title: From Inhibitor to Reporter: Nirmatrelvir-Derived Fluorogenic Substrates for the SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease.
papers.summary: A library of fluorogenic SARS-CoV-2 main protease substrates derived from nirmatrelvir and a parent substrate yielded compound 6 with about ten-fold improved catalytic efficiency (kcat/KM 21,400 M-1 s-1). It enabled kinetic characterization of three potent Mpro inhibitors, supporting next-generation COVID-19 drug development.

papers.title: Role of estrogen-related receptor alpha in osteogenic differentiation.
papers.summary: ERRα overexpression enhanced extracellular matrix mineralization in osteoblasts and aortic valve interstitial cells, while suppression reduced mineralization and RUNX2/NOTCH3 expression. In endothelial cells, ERRα maintained viability and inflammatory/metabolic homeostasis rather than directly driving differentiation, highlighting a therapeutic target for impaired bone formation and pathological calcification.

papers.title: GMPS promotes cervical squamous cell carcinoma cell immune evasion through USP7-mediated deubiquitination of PDL1.
papers.summary: GMPS is elevated in cervical squamous cell carcinoma; knockdown suppressed proliferation, enhanced CD8+ T-cell cytotoxicity, reduced PD-L1, and inhibited xenograft growth. GMPS interacts with USP7 and positively regulates it, promoting PD-L1 deubiquitination and stability, identifying GMPS as a promising immunotherapy target in cervical cancer.

papers.title: Functional conservation of divergent peptidase_M60 O-glycopeptidases in Enterococcus.
papers.summary: Two divergent peptidase_M60 enzymes from Enterococcus faecium and Enterococcus faecalis show both mucinase and O-glycopeptidase activity despite distant sequence similarity to characterized homologs. Structural analysis of EfmM60 reveals active-site features accommodating extended, branched O-glycans, demonstrating broad functional conservation within this highly divergent enzyme family.

papers.title: Nervous System Integrity in Drosophila: Essential and Dosage-Sensitive Roles of Hsp110.
papers.summary: Drosophila Hsp110 is dispensable for larval cell proliferation but essential for long-term neuronal survival and nervous system development, with loss causing ubiquitin-positive brain inclusions. Overexpression is detrimental, mimicking Hsp40 overexpression; chaperone levels must be balanced, and the Hsp70 network should be targeted as a whole.

papers.title: Same sex chromosomes with independent origins in haplochromine cichlids.
papers.summary: Whole-genome sequencing of Tropheini cichlids reveals sex chromosomes on LG5 and LG7 repeatedly co-opted across haplochromines but independently originated. Gene function, allele differences, and sex-biased expression show no evidence that sexual antagonism drove LG5 evolution; sex-determining genes or mechanisms likely differ despite shared chromosomes.

papers.title: Loss of LRRK2 Protects Against Ox-LDL-Induced Endothelial Oxidative Damage Via NRF2.
papers.summary: LRRK2 upregulates in oxidized LDL-treated HUVECs; silencing improves survival, reduces apoptosis and reactive oxygen species, restores mitochondrial membrane potential, and activates NRF2 signaling with increased HO-1 and NQO1. NRF2 inhibition with ML385 reverses protection, implicating LRRK2 inhibition against atherosclerotic endothelial dysfunction.

papers.title: Accounting for recombination rate variation improves inference of barrier loci and reveals the role of both natural and sexual selection in an incipient bird radiation.
papers.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
papers.summary: Recombination-aware analyses of reunion gray white-eye forms show putative divergent selection targets concentrated on the Z chromosome, except between ecologically distinct forms. Barrier loci link to song formation and immune function between similar niches, or altitude and morphology between different niches, implicating both natural and sexual selection.

papers.title: Mutation rate variation as the neutral byproduct of developmental and life-history diversification.
papers.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
papers.summary: A life-history hypothesis proposes generational mutation rates diversify passively with developmental and life-history traits, without selection on mutator alleles. Developmental models and simulations show the observed negative population size-mutation rate correlation arises neutrally; mammalian phylogenetics supports covariation between body mass, generation time, and mutation rate as sufficient.

papers.title: Museum genomics links MC1R alleles to adaptive winter coat color polymorphism in the long-tailed weasel.
papers.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
papers.summary: Using museum specimens of long-tailed weasels, genome-wide association identified a single genomic region containing MC1R linked to winter coat color polymorphism. Three MC1R alleles with distinct amino acid deletions associate independently with winter brown morphs on the west and east coasts, showing recurrent camouflage evolution.

papers.title: Specificity and Regulatory Mechanism of Metal Ions in Cas12a Enzymatic Cleavage Activity.
papers.summary: Various metal ions significantly affect Cas12a cleavage activity and specificity, mediating enzyme-substrate binding by increasing Cas12a affinity for single-stranded DNA. Uniquely, Mn2+ enables cleavage by activating only the catalytic domain without the entire enzyme. Structural and mutagenesis analyses clarify metal-dependent catalysis, informing Cas12a-based biotechnology.

papers.title: ACOD1-dependent succinate signalling acts as a metabolic checkpoint for osteoclast differentiation.
papers.summary: ACOD1 overexpression in RAW264.7 cells shifted metabolism toward glycolysis and impaired osteoclastogenesis while keeping NFATc1 nuclear and inducing inflammatory genes. Extracellular succinate activates NFATC1 via GPR91-Gαq signaling, and ACOD1 promotes an innate immune transcriptional program, positioning succinate-GPR91 signaling as a checkpoint between inflammation and osteoclast differentiation.

papers.title: Impact of BCL-2 rs2279115 and rs3943258 variants on protein expression and clinical outcome of urothelial bladder carcinoma.
papers.summary: In urothelial bladder carcinoma, the BCL-2 rs2279115 variant associates with BCL-2-positive expression (TT and GT genotypes), and the CT haplotype independently associates with high-grade tumors. BCL-2 genotyping, haplotype structure, and immunohistochemical expression may complement risk assessment, pending prospective clinical validation.

papers.title: UPS-mediated P-glycoprotein regulation in Alzheimer's disease: pharmacological implications for the amyloid pathology.
papers.summary: This review examines how ubiquitin-proteasome system-mediated P-glycoprotein regulation drives impaired amyloid-beta clearance across the blood-brain barrier in Alzheimer's disease. Amyloid-beta, oxidative stress, and inflammatory signaling promote P-gp phosphorylation, ubiquitination, internalization, and degradation, compromising transporter function and barrier integrity, with evidence linking altered P-gp turnover to disease progression.

papers.title: Vitamin E treatment modulates steatotic and attenuates oxidative stress in a MASLD in vitro model.
papers.summary: In a biomimetic co-culture of HuH-7 and LX-2 cells on liver extracellular matrix hydrogel, MASLD was induced with oleic and palmitic acid. Vitamin E improved viability, reduced lipid accumulation, activated NRF2 antioxidant signaling, and suppressed LX-2 activation via TGF-beta inhibition, providing a physiologically relevant drug screening model.
